22515.d:
An important element of generative art is emergence. The most famous algorithm for this is probably Cellular Automata (CA).

However, numerous generative artists have created works using CA, which has lost its visual freshness and is like chewing gum that has lost its taste.

Although it is such a classic algorithm, adding my own little ideas to it and finding a new "flavor" is the reason why I code.

Here, the subject is 1D Elementary Cellular Automata, the simplest of all cellular automata. 1D Elementary Cellular Automata has 256 different rules, which change the shapes produced. This work aims to create more complex shapes by randomly selecting some of those rules and placing multiple of them on the screen.

The on/off of the CA cell is often likened to the behavior of living creatures.As of 2022, in the country where I live, prices are rising, wages are not increasing, and COVID-19 has not yet ended. I created this work with the image of people at the mercy of these various rules.

---

S key: Save png
L key: Show/hide grid

22516.d:
A super rare interactive light sculpture from the 1970s acquires new life in the virtual world, transformed into its digital twin with a generative NFTs collection delivered to the blockchain.

Programma is a generative image-composition NFT collection by artist Francesca Fini. In this collection, the artist created the official digital re-enactment of the interactive light sculpture “Programma” conceived in the 70s by her father, the modernist designer Gianfranco Fini, and produced in a very limited edition by the visionary Italian company New Lamp. 

The original 70s IRL light sculpture is a stainless steel piece measuring 104X104 cm, with a backlit opaque methacrylate panel and 100 movable plates. The interactive manual opening and closing of the plates can create infinite light patterns and combinations. The piece is featured in “Luce lampade 1968-1973: il nuovo design italiano”, by Fulvio Ferrari e Napoleone Ferrari, Allemandi Editore. 

New Lamp was one of the most innovative manufacturers of lighting in Italy at the end of the 1960s. Founded in Rome in 1968 by Mario Vento and his brother Gianni. Working with artists, architects, and graphic designers to develop original lighting designs, the company produced experimental lamps that were akin to works of art yet entirely functional designs.

While the precise number of Programma lights produced was never documented, the design was one of the more ambitious and expensive works by New Lamp and very few originals are known, often sold for tens of thousands of dollars at Christie's and other major auction houses.
In this generative collection, Francesca Fini works on the binary concepts of full and empty, off and on, which are the basis of the original IRL sculpture, transforming them into the digital variants that make up the infinite combinations randomly created at minting.

https://www.francescafini.com/programma

What Is Brutalism?
Brutalism is a style of architecture that lasted from the 1950s-1970s, and it was characterized by simple, block-like, hulking concrete structures, with an emphasis on materials, textures and construction, producing highly expressive forms.

The buildings are characterised by their massive, monolithic and ‘blocky’ appearance with a rigid geometric style and large-scale use of poured concrete.

Brutalism began to fade out in the 1980s, where it increasingly came to be regarded as cold, alienating and unfit for humans. It turned out that concrete had an allure of indestructibility but deteriorated from the inside, making it difficult to maintain and prone to crumbling and water damage as it aged.

In the years since, the world has been divided into those who think that Brutalist buildings are eyesores that should be demolished and those who find these vintage but not yet historic buildings architectural masterpieces to be cherished and preserved. 

--------------------------------------------------------
About the work:
This work was built entirely with code using only math, logic and 2D shapes to create light, shadow and perspective.

--------------------------------------------------------
Features:
"Canvas Orientation": Square, Portrait
"Building Size": Large, Medium, Small
"Time of day": Day, Night
"Sun/Moon": True, False
"Palette": 23 palettes
"Floors": 3, 4
"Clouds": True, False

--------------------------------------------------------
Constrols in live mode:
On desktop: Press 's' or 'S' to save as PNG (2622x3720 or 3720x3720)
On mobile: Touch the screen to save as PNG (2622x3720 or 3720x3720)

The harmonic aspect of the composition is based on the application of various scales and chords - often derived from a central tonality - that are layered and interleaved in a manner similar to the visual shapes of the piece. This creates a constantly shifting harmonic landscape that is both familiar and unpredictable.

The rhythmic element of the composition is based on the layering of multiple polyrhythms, creating a complex and ever-shifting pulse. The polyrhythms are often based on a central pulse that is then layered and interleaved with other polyrhythms to create a complex and dynamic rhythmical landscape.

Overall, the pieces are designed to explore the relationships between shapes, harmonies, and rhythms in a way that is both logical and unexpected. The goal is to create a composition that is both cohesive and unpredictable, allowing for an ever-evolving soundscape of sound and movement.

'Look. at. yourself.
You are in my art.
You are the central figure of the work of art!' - @m5alien


The Look. at. yourself. conceptual generative project is a new step in the m5alien's exploration of the territory of the artist, the viewer and the algorithm co-authorship; this is the viewer's invitation to another dimension, where he becomes the central figure in the joint being created work of art.

Co-authorship takes place at three levels: visual, actual, and algorithmic.

Visual level
This is the space of the artist, where she uses the viewer’s reflection to create an artistic image.

Actual level
This is the viewer's area; each edition in the collection is a living piece that exists when the viewer looks at it.

Algorithmic level
The generative algorithm creates a unique art capsule with certain parameters for each edition: loop duration, aspect ratio, orientation, frame rate, and the epistle*. All this data after minting can be seen in the section 'Features'.
*The epistle is the vibe of the artwork; a dialog between the artist and the viewer under the direction of a generative algorithm.

After the launch of the collection, 105 editions will be visible as reserved (artist's reserve). In the first year after the release, as many editions will be open to collectors as the age of the artist. Further, each year of the artist's life will be marked by the unlocking of one artwork.

22538.d:
A tower for playing Jenga, assembled and disassembled, moving, growing, breaking, and so on.
But all this is just an illusion on the display.

This is the third part of the interpretation of Jenga through generative art. If we are already working in the digital space, why not go beyond some boundaries and conditions of physical space?

In this work, I created the illusion of a three-dimensional space by constructing figures on a plane using the principles of descriptive geometry and the rules for constructing perspective with two convergence points. I also tried to create a generating color palette and set the movement of objects. No pre-made palettes or WEBGL.

22547.d:
Eye floaters are spots in your vision which often happen as people age. 

This image consists of the interactions of two distinct sets of algorithms.

The background: Imagine a barbershop floor where one strand of hair has fallen after being cut from every human's head on the planet. If you sorted through those hairs and organized them into groups of color you would find that approximately 2% are red, approximately 5% are blond, approximately 11% are brown or auburn and the rest, approximately 82%, are black or dark brown. 

The background image is made up of randomly placed algorithmically generated spirals or curls, or locks of hair. Random numbers are assigned to variables for number of turns, translation (location) and rotation of each curl. The total number of curls is arbitrary, but the color percentages of curls will stay the same no matter how may curls are drawn.

The foreground: A single "tile" consisting of concentric circles where a smaller inner circle knocks a hole out of the larger outer circle that contains it. A semi-transparent radial gradient of random colors, colors each shape. A regular grid of these tiles are drawn on top of the background. Occasionally one or more tile is allowed to drop out of the grid. The placement of each inner circle in each tile in the array is based on an overlying algorithm. Within the hole opened up by the smaller circle a nearly circular "pupil" is placed; it is a single random solid color and it provides a structure to the image. The background shows through the "iris" of each eyeball, around the tiles and the edges of the array and where a few tiles have dropped out. 

The juxtaposition of the grid of semi-transparent tiles over the hairy background present a frenetic image. It is visually complex, rich with micro and macro interactions. Enjoy

Please visit www.drbillkolomyjec.com

22566.d:
One year ago, I published my first Fx(hash) work, "Finding my way". This piece marks its anniversary, and is intended as a THANK YOU to all the people that collected my works. 

It is based on the same algorithm as "Finding my way", i.e. a line growth animated process based on Substrate (Jared Tarbell, 2003) guided by dynamically changing vector fields made with trigonometric functions, but it uses different palettes, more vector fields, and a few more tweakings of the algorithm parameters.

The original piece was intended to symbolise a person's process of finding her/his way. Upon further reflections on the result, I think it more as representing a community process. So here is my wish for the Fx(hash) community, let's keep on finding our way.   

In what now could become a tradition, I've stolen again a palette from the beautiful work of Iskra Velitchkova.

Implemented using various packages from thi.ng/umbrella by Karsten Schmidt, AKA Toxi

22568.d:
THIS IS NOT AN ARTWORK.

Instead: a framework to store artwork data components onchain by including them as features in the token's smart contract. The stored data are parameters of a Lindenmayer System, which is a formal grammar that was initially conceived of as a theory of plant growth. L-Systems can model complex forms of plants using relatively few simple rules. Custom rules are generated during the minting of each token, based on the transaction hash string. 

The idea is that each iteration of the artwork can be reproduced accurately using an L-System interpreter by accessing the tezos blockchain through the FxHash API (GraphQL) and interpreting token metadata.

Reusable template source: https://github.com/x-terrain/x-terrain.github.io/tree/main/L-Template

Part of an ongoing project with RefractionDAO

22604.d:
Modern art is derived from the surrounding environment. What is important is the artist's perception of his surroundings. Modernism is an idea that emphasizes the power of man to create, improve and change the shape of his environment, using science, technology and practical experiments.
Along with modern art, the role of traditional elements of my surroundings has been used in this collection. In general, the motif is actually an abstraction of the face of nature and reaching simple forms. The motif is used in painting, visual arts, drama, literature, music and architecture, and it can have its cultural identifiers in various sciences. With a little study in different motifs, you can understand what symbols or pictorial roots are used in their culture. The role of the subject in each scientific and artistic field has a different definition and concept, but basically, at the core of all definitions and fields, it is ultimately the concept of modeling.
This is the pattern of the old materials of the historical places of Iran that I have photographed.

22607.d:
A frozen scene from a lost dimension
An alternative of where we once were, or where we will be 
Caught in the moment and set in place
Between all states
Static pixels on a digital canvas

The path to this collection has created many alternatives lost in time themselves. It began as a study of points of light, with geometric objects in the background. The background objects developed a life of their own and then birds, and ships, made out of bezier shapes became the focal points. Then everything got lost in clouds before the collection as it stands now emerged. Aside from the published traits, many of the artifacts created on the way are still generated. For example, star fields, birds, sonars and gas bubbles. These are sometimes visible, but when they appear, it is simply by some chaotic chance.

This collection has been coded with P5js and WebGL. Half of all primary sales proceeds, and secondary royalties, are assigned to the Processing Foundation.

Dear collectors,
Rings was originally published as Project #10921 on March 19, 2022.
(https://www.fxhash.xyz/generative/10921)
Due to a technical issue, Project #10921 has been hidden from the site and is being replaced by this reissued version.

_______________________________

Rings project in its first version was made at an unfavorable time and had technical problems that resulted in outputs far from my idealization as a creator. This re-edition opportunity allowed me not only to correct the offline library access problems, but also to implement what I actually envisioned in this work.

Technically, Rings consists of the aesthetic result of the radial accumulation of simple shapes (circles, squares and triangles) acting as small particles that follow polar functions to form concentric patterns that are not always so symmetrical.

While the backgrounds are filled with more sober colors, the front palettes are the result of the trichromatic combination inspired by Brazilian biomes, in homage to our rich geographic diversity. The trail left by these particles allows the formation of a type of "brush texture" on the canvas, while shadows and white dots give the necessary finish, helping with depth perception.

And again....palletes carefully chosen.

> Foreground Palette: Pampas Grassland, Cerrado Savanna, Amazon Rainforest, Atlantic Coast, Caatinga Dry Forest, Pantanal Wetlands, Atlantic Forest
> Background Palette: 5 'sober' colors.
> Radius Shape: Round, Oval-X, Oval-Y.
> Trail Rate: 0.25, 0.33, 0.5, 1.0 Hz.
> Total Particles Amount: 400, 600, 800, 1000.
> Offscreen Frames: 200, 300, 400, 500, 600.

> Discover!

J'ai trouvé un cahier l'autre jour dans une vieille école. Plus personne n'y va depuis des lustres, dans cette école. Elle a fermé il y a peut-être trente ans. C'est d'abord la poste qui est partie. Puis le bar, il n'y avait plus assez de clients, même les ivrognes locaux ne suffisaient pas. L'école elle est restée parce que la maire a tout fait pour. Mais au bout d'un moment elle est partie et l'école avec.

Dans le cahier il y a plein de dessins de différentes époques. C'est toujours des arbres mais comme dessinés toujours avec simplement des lignes. Pas d'effets, juste des lignes droites faites au crayon ou au stylo. Des générations d'écoliers qui se sont refilés le cahier pour dessiner plutôt que de faire de la grammaire. 

C'est marrant parce qu'il y a des dates sur chaque page du cahier. Il y a des dessins qui datent d'avant les guerres. Plus la date est loin, plus le tronc est grand, plus le feuillage est fourni. Les arbres, on dirait qu'ils continuent de grandir avec le temps.

Stroboscopic uses the hash to assign one of 23 designs to each mint, then assigns colors from 26 color palettes. As each Stroboscopic runs, colors rapidly cycle and create patterns than are perceived as movement. Sometimes there are only subtle variations in color that create changes that are barely discernible. Other times, the shifting of colors and contrast can be quite vibrant and even difficult to watch, as patterns of movement develop and shift rapidly. Patterns shift, pause and sometimes repeat, sometimes predictable but often totally out of control.

RELEASE the LEFT MOUSE BUTTON to resume activity.

Type ‘s’ or ‘S’ to save a screen capture.

The ability to pause and capture an image while the sketch runs allows the viewer to create an almost infinite number of different still images.

Instead ink, brush, and rice paper, rectangles, p5js and screen, explores not code realism, but code-ism composition and form. 畫, painting, each landscape is performed, unknowing the exact, as is Chinese landscape painting, the painter, paints his or her fictional landscape. Here my code and the hash paints each landscape with a constrained brush, that is rectangles. 

An important aesthetic factor in Chinese landscape painting is the negative space. Here the positive-negative relation is akin to ying-yang, that in Tai-Chi (太極), there are no absolute positive-yang and absolute negative-ying. At the edge of one polar extreme, signals the change towards the other. Like midday, the sun will set. And between midday and midnight, there is plenty of grey.

22644.d:
Digitally crafted flowers in pots for virtual window sills.

In the spirit of the piranha plant from the Mario Bros videogame. We wanted to create a project that acknowledges the playful depiction of nature in early videogames by creating a retro futuristic collectible that explores aesthetics over gameplay, whilst preserving the playful energy of these early digital worlds. There are many game elements that have emerged over the years that have become iconic in their own right. Their memorable designs have come to represent the exciting feeling of when we first discovered these worlds, but over time an appreciation for their simple design execution, harmony and balance has emerged. Art can exist in many forms and places including a digital pot plant.

Rarity:

There are a total of 23 hand-drawn and animated sprites divided into 4 groups Firelillies, Flytraps, Quasars and Stargazers and there are 15 possible combinations made from these 4 groups. 18% of the collection is a combination of these 4 groups which we can call random and the remaining 72% is divided between the remaining 14 combinations.


There are 3 possible grid systems 1x1, 3x3 and 4x4 

3% 1x1

40% 3x3

57% 4x4



There are 14 possible placement points for all grids and 76 stem/sprite arragement in total



For the pots and stems there are 11 colors to choose and  no rarities for color combinations.



The flower distribution can be either symmetric or random. 35% symmetric and 65% random



Export options:

Pressing 's' on desktop or holding for 2 seconds will download gif to whatever the current device resolution is. To export at a different resolution open the token in new window by clicking 'open' link under the token image and add "&exportsize=1080" or "&exportsize=2160" to end of the url and hit enter then either hold for 2 seconds or press 's' to create gif and download.

Dear collectors,
Intricate 4x4 was originally published as Project #12851 on May 12, 2022.
(https://www.fxhash.xyz/generative/12851)
Due to a technical issue, Project #12851 has been hidden from the site and is being replaced by this reissued version.

_______________________________

'Intricated 4x4' was a projects that took me time to develop. With each WIP, I realized that I could improve some detail, some feature looking for more pleasant, democratic and varied aesthetic results.

This work consists of generating four sets of particles (ellipses or squares) that appear in the four corners of the screen, respecting the predefined margin limits. These sets move towards the center following an attenuated decrease in size thanks to the combination of logarithm and mapping of frameCount and the size variable. This simple trick ensures smoother and less aggressive movements, bringing the observer a sense of tranquility.

Combining the use of different palettes with some movement conditionals - functions back() and go() - and a charming touch of shading and depth, 'Intricated 4x4' can be considered one of my favorite
works and I hope it will be for you, after the mint.

Palletes carefully chosen =)

_______________________________
Variability of editions is ensured by:
* 8 background colors
* 13 palettes x 4 colors = 52 colors picked one by one with a lot of care
* possibility to have a fantastic BW version (rarity: 5%)
* possibility to repeat the same palette for both sets (rarity: 8%)
* possibility to have squares intead of circles (rarity: 25%)
* a wide range of Shapes number
* a well thought number of frames, proportional to the total frameCount to make things 'softer'

_______________________________
Interactive instructions:
* Press [S] to save your .png file
* Press [P] to play/pause your animation anytime you like (this increase exponentially your possibilities, right!?).

22655.d:
Yet Another Noises and Flows

After three works on landscapes I returned to an abstract work in which I used several kinds of noise fields and a different approach to flow lines.

In this work I use three intermediate images to generate the final image:
- on the first image to each pixels is assigned a color related to the value of the noise field in that point using the main color palette
- on the second image the gradient orientation (angle) of the field is used to assign colors using a secondary palette with the purpose of giving lights and shadows to the final image
- on the third image flow lines are drawn using the direction perpendicular to the gradient, in this way the flows are aligned to the contour lines

After the second and third step the new generated image is blended with the previous giving rise to the final image.

Developed with p5.js

Default resolution: 2400x1600, 1600x2400, 2000x2000 (3/2, 2/3, 1/1 aspect ratio)

[2] to redraw at double resolution (it takes four times then default)
[1] to redraw at default resolution
[s] to save a png at current resolution

Sources of variations are:
- 14 palettes
- 6 kinds of combinations of noise type and fractal type
- 8 kinds of cuts
- 3 kinds of aspect ratio
- 3 border thickness

This Generative Token uses the FastNoiseLite.js and chroma.js libraries.

22669.d:
The title of this image composition draw from the Persian word “heech,” which translates to “nothing.” The word is composed of three Persian letters, he, ye, and če. While at first glance the artwork connotation appears vague, several layers of meaning can be derived from artist representation of “nothingness.” The first, as stated by the artist, is associated with the belief, in Persian sufism, that “God created the universe out of nothing” and that “nothingness is everywhere.”

The term is sometimes used in association with anomie to explain the general mood of despair at a perceived pointlessness of existence or arbitrariness of human principles and social institutions. Nihilism has also been described as conspicuous in or constitutive of certain historical periods. For example, Jean Baudrillard and others have characterized postmodernity as a nihilistic epoch or mode of thought. Likewise, some theologians and religious figures have stated that postmodernity and many aspects of modernity represent nihilism by a negation of religious principles. Nihilism has, however, been widely ascribed to both religious and irreligious viewpoints.

This collection is 1000x1000px 300dpi, consists of combining three main dimensions and repeating the word "nothing" 4 times in 7 different colors, and the artist's goal is to create a competition to mint NFT's on the page of the work from nothing and lose color to complete blackness.


Note: I suggest you to google it for more information about "heech"

Dear collectors,
Extrusion was originally published as Project #14512 on June 9, 2022.
(https://www.fxhash.xyz/generative/14512)
Due to a technical issue, Project #14512 has been hidden from the site and is being replaced by this reissued version.

_______________________________

Extrusion is a work that brings the generation of particles that perform smooth sinusoidal movements according to the evolution of the animation frames. Each frame registers its position with a slight shading, and with continuous stacking we get the impression of depth that I like to call 'pseudo-3D'.
The perception of movement is something that I really enjoy watching and I hope it can have the same effect on collectors and enthusiasts of animated arts. Even so, for those who prefer static art, the work is finished after a frame count (which may vary depending on its hash) by adding a grain texture followed by a thin black beveled frame with white passe-partout for better highlighting. the post-animation result.

The palette sets were carefully chosen, totaling 19 palettes with 6 colors each, separated into themes of environment, mood, styles, materials and other elements. Of these seven are monochromatic sets with a small rarity of being obtained.

The shapes of the particles vary between 8 pointed stars (rare), circles and vertical or horizontal bars and their trail changes a lot according to the frame count and total number of objects in the scene. Sometimes they look like they are dancing while moving around creating pseudo-three-dimensional objects.

The screens can be obtained in three different aspect ratios: 1x1 (square, more common), and two wide options (16x9 landscape and 9x16 portrait, a little rarer).

As already said and I always say: carefully chosen palettes!

_______________________________
Variety of editions is guaranteed by several features:
* Black or white backgrounds (for better highlighting of particles);
* 19 color palettes with 6 colors each where the rarest is BW (<6%)
* 3 aspect ratios: 1x1 (50%), 9x16 (25%) and 16x9 (25%)
* Controlled variety of scale;
* Controlled variety of particle number;
* Animation time;
* Shape type: circles (60%), bars (30%) and stars (10%);
* Animation with coordinated movement (12%);
* Super rare inverted move (5%)

_______________________________
Interactive instructions:
* Press [I] to change the inverted mode, if you have it.

_______________________________
Saving your .png file:
* Press [S] to save your .png file in screen size;
* Press [0] to save your .png file in qHD resolution;
* Press [1] to save your .png file in FHD resolution;
* Press [2] to save your .png file in UHD (4K) resolution;
* Press [3] to save your .png file in FUHD (8K) resolution;
(for higher resolutions, please wait up for few seconds until complete render)


Made with p5.js

22703.d:
In astronomy, kosmos refers to the entire physical cosmos as a cohesive whole (from the Greek kosmos, which means "order," "harmony," and "the world"). Humanity's increasing comprehension of all the things and occurrences in the universe.

To understand how the world works, we must first investigate the fundamental components of our existence - time, space, energy and matter - and how they operate under the extraordinary physical conditions that define the infant and evolving Universe.

Scientists, particularly astrophysicists, are directly tackling fundamental issues concerning the nature of complicated astrophysical phenomena such as black holes, neutron stars, dark energy, and gravitational waves. Their ultimate, overarching objective is to learn more about the genesis and purpose of existence of the cosmos by employing a fleet of space-based missions operating across the whole electromagnetic spectrum.

The universe is largely made up of both helium and hydrogen. Indeed, these two elements account for 98% of all observable substance in the cosmos. Nonetheless, our planet and everything in it—even life itself—are only imaginable due to the presence of heavier elements including iron, silicon, oxygen, nitrogen, carbon, and a plethora of others.

However, all of this comprehension leaded through the quest of the meaning of the cosmos, which originated with the emergence of life, will vanish with its conclusion. That leaves us only one realization: we are responsible with discovering our own meaning during our brief stint in the sun.

We began this composition by creating coloured pencil strokes. We then made rhombuses and arranged them in different ways. It wasn't until the work was nearly complete that we realised we were creating the view from our desk, looking out through the window into the garden. Sky, clouds, leaves, fence posts, reflections on the glass and a large ceramic star hanging.

There are 4 layers which may or may not be visible as default but which can be toggled with the keyboard:
b - set a dark background to the whole piece
w - weather - each piece has the potential for either rain, snow or wind
c - cloud or sunburst
s - star
Number keys render the image at increasing resolutions up to 7

Exactly one year ago I was minting my first fxhash project. 
“Posizioni” was a quick sketch of only 25 editions that I put together to test this new platform and to my great surprise, it was the start of an amazing journey in this space that still continues to amaze me every day. 

“RE/Posizioni” is an ideal continuation of my personal path that started one year ago: I decided to create an animated, glitchy, or even broken piece, something completely different from what I usually do as an artist and as a coder (and probably something I’m not very good at, forgive me for this :D ).
Even if this NFT crazy world is often uncertain, insecure, or unstable, we need to find a balance no matter how difficult, just as the lines in this artwork try to do.

Going out of my comfort zone, experimenting, or just having fun is what keeps this creative practice enjoyable for me, and it’s all that matters.

22730.d:
Initially described in 1704, Truchet's method of placing rotated tiles in a repeating pattern has been developed and iterated on for years, including the classic 10 PRINT maze. An article on multi-scale Truchet tiles caught my eye: https://christophercarlson.com/portfolio/multi-scale-truchet-patterns/ features a clear and easy-to-follow 'recipe' for the production of multi-scale tilings. I initially implemented the algorithm as shown, and began iterating. What if the region of the tile that repeated (the central part of the tile as opposed to what the article calls ‘wings’) was of variable size, or greater than the size of the tile itself? What if the rotation of the tile was not limited to multiples of ninety degrees? What if an inverse tile was created that replaced the tile for certain points on the grid.

And so the piece evolved. Where ‘The Elegant Void’ was all about circles, contrast and bold, bright colour palettes, ‘The Elegant Plane’ shifts to the repeated tiling of the plane, based on and inspired by the Truchet tile.

A note concerning browsers: Somewhat idiosyncratically, the live render in Safari does not always match the live render in Chrome, and therefore the site-generated preview. The differences are subtle, but users of browsers other than Chrome should be aware. The charitable collector might even consider this a feature, rather than an unusually-stubborn quirk of considerable chagrin to the artist…

22733.d:
The word affects and reshapes land in an eternal cycle.

The development of this series invited me to cross the land through songs and glyphs and to discover the Manding languages script: N'Ko. It is a cables.gl patch that blends procedural terrains and text strings made from 8 letters whose order is continuously randomized (it takes some time, be patient).

The piece has some controls:
- Use 1, 2, 3 and 4 to change the view.
- Use P to open the performance panel.
- Use S to download a black and white image of the terrain to use as height map or to hear it using PIXELSYNTH (https://ojack.xyz/PIXELSYNTH/)

A more detailed article about this artwork can be found here: https://www.fxhash.xyz/article/bankoo-or-nko-or-u%2B07c0-u%2B07ff ⛰️

The Mandelbrot set is a mathematical object that is generated by a simple formula, and it exhibits some interesting visual patterns that are reminiscent of those found in nature, such as the self-similarity of branching structures, the repetition of small-scale patterns on larger scales, and the presence of chaotic behavior.

The beauty of Polaroid film lies in its ability to capture and preserve a moment in space and time in a unique and tangible way.

This work combines two things that are incongruent with each other and brings them together to create a digital memory that serves as a reminder that complexity can be found even in the simplest things, that art is intrinsic to nature itself.

• press '1' to scale the photo to 1024x1024 pixels (the default output)
• press '2' to scale the photo to 2048x2048 pixels (Warning: can be slow!)
• press '3' to scale the photo to 4096x4096 pixels (Warning: can be very slow!)
• press 'd' to save the Mandelbrot Set
• press 's' to save the Polaroid film

Done with p5.js

22739.d:
The Enfantines are three sets of beginner piano pieces by Erik Satie, written with the aim of preparing children for the sound patterns of modern music. Composed in 1913, these are genuine children’s pieces, crafted for small hands, easy to learn. 

“Enfantines II. Enfantillages Pittoresques” is the second of a set of algorithms that explore the basics of Generative Art, written with the aim of preparing artists for the script patterns of digital life. “Enfantillages Pittoresques” experiments with predefined plots, colour blending, webgl shaders, and generative music; all with a fresh, childish style. This algorithm has been trained to draw basic shapes in accordance to Satie’s lyrics. However, it uses them in unusual ways and creates what looks like fantastic creatures, microscopic beings, or, to follow Corneille, Constant, and Appel: "human animals".

“It took me four years to paint like Raphael, but a lifetime to paint like a child” Attributed to Picasso (falsely, probably)

With two modes that won’t produce the same outputs, “Enfantines” are best experienced twice. In music mode, the code uses Satie’s piano composition as a way of taming randomness, the sounds affecting the parameters of the strokes.

Hey, these have won me congratulations from the Shah of Persia and the King of Yvetot!


# INTERACTIVITY
Press M or Double Tap (mobile) for AUDIO mode
Wait for SILENT mode
Press I for Trait Info (desktop)
Press 1 for Canvas Save (desktop)

Introduce “?pixelDensity=171” after URL for FULL SCREEN MODE (pseudo-deterministic).
Introduce “?pixelDensity=X” for HQ renders (standard is 2, and 8 produces 400ppi 40x44cm prints).


# EASY-TO-READ CODE
The “Enfantines” are educational algorithms. The code has been compressed and minified for a performance boost, but can be read fully in GitHub: https://github.com/ratchitect/


# PERFORMANCE
Better experienced with Chrome.

Inspiration:

I had the chance to flip @carson's handoff piece, Sigil Squared. I knew I wanted to keep the same palette, line structure, and mirroring of some kind. I love how Sigil Squared pulses into different shapes before stopping, but I wanted to try to turn the animation into a slow and angular pixel lava lamp. By far the most difficult part was trying to squeeze every last character in the tweetcart. I had to make some sacrifices with the pixel burning effect around the lines, but ended with a trig offset that I quite liked. 

If you're interested, the Tweetcart Relay is a series of tweetcarts minted and passed between artists who take the prior work, and modify it to their liking. Anyone who likes to make tweetcarts or wants to learn how can join!

Relay information:
-> inspiration tweetcart: Sigil Squared; https://www.fxhash.xyz/generative/slug/sigil-squared
-> inspiration tweetcart author: carson; tz1XqJ9e6NdouxdGvm2V3aknwFnGL6Kinu6A
-> destination tweetcart author: aebrer; tz1ZBMhTa7gxSpaeXoqyc6bTCrxEHfZYSpPt

Pico-8 Source Code:
-> 149 Tokens, 270 Characters

``` Lua
-- alexthescott
-- bad fuzz
-- 22/12/16

-- fxhash()
rng = stat(6)
if rng == "" then
rng=tostr(rnd(-1)\1)..","..tostr(1+rnd(3)\1)..","..tostr(rnd(16)\1)..","
end
rng_vals = {}
c_num = ""
for i=1,#rng do
 if sub(rng,i,i) != "," then
  c_num = c_num..sub(rng,i,i)
 else 
  add(rng_vals,tonum(c_num))
  c_num = ""
 end
end

--tweetcart
poke(24364,5)r=rnd
z=r(.0004)p=.5+r(2)+5e=r(9)+1g=8f=128n=cos
for i=0,7do pal(i,(r{8,-7,9,10,11,12,140}),1)end::♥::g+=z
for i=0,768do
x=r(f)y=r(f)pset(x-n(x),y-n(y),max(pget(x,y)-1,0))end
for i=0,32do
m=(p+n(g))*7
line(n(n(g/p-i/32))*m+64,n(n(g/7-i/7))*m+64,i)end
goto ♥
```
